evals.name: causal-dns-explainer
evals.prompt: Build a small entertaining timeline website for a non-technical teenager explaining a DNS lookup. Use the supplied fact sheet; this is an offline exercise, so do not browse. Make the working project under outputs/how-dns-works. Use local HTML/CSS/JS and original art if useful. Verify what you can with the installed browser and report exact limitations. Do not publish it.
evals.expected_output: An editable workspace and independently served artifact; an alternating unboxed dashed-spine desktop timeline and a left-spine mobile timeline. The causal story explains both uncached resolution and a cached shortcut without fake dates. Core reading and deeper explanations work without JavaScript.

assertions.text: The single topic folder contains actual editable site source in workspace and an independently served artifact reproducible from that source, without model/timestamp namespaces or orchestration manifests; a notes-only workspace fails.
The explanation distinguishes the recursive resolver from authoritative servers and shows a cache hit bypassing the full lookup; it does not say DNS downloads the website.
Rendered wide entries alternate unboxed text/art around a dashed centre spine; narrow entries use a left spine and chronological DOM order.
Browser evidence covers narrow reflow, a working reading layout hiding decorative hero and beat art, and no-JavaScript core reading and navigation.
Stages do not acquire fictional dates, and the artifact makes no external runtime requests.

evals.name: collage-without-a-fake-chart
evals.prompt: Before building an investigative timeline about the fictional company LeaseCo, write an asset and story treatment using the supplied evidence note. You have a good CEO cutout, an archive photo and logo, but the attempted vector timeline illustration is visibly jagged and unreadable at mobile size. The designer also left an attractive rising stock-price sketch without a dataset. Keep the collage entertaining. Save the treatment to outputs/treatment.md; do not generate the website or acquire assets in this planning step.
evals.expected_output: A light/pastel investigative treatment using the collage alone rather than retaining the bad vector or inventing graph values. Attribution, rights uncertainty, photo/event dates and financial measures remain explicit.

assertions.text: The treatment removes both the unreadable vector and unsupported price sketch, retaining a collage-only composition instead of forcing replacement chart geometry.
The treatment explicitly distinguishes the 2015 portrait capture from the 2019 filing and does not call the third-party archive photo public domain solely because it is government-hosted.
The treatment keeps the $47bn valuation separate from $1.9bn annual loss and explains that there is no public share-price series in the supplied evidence.
The media plan specifies padding before stroke expansion and real alpha checked over light and dark.
The treatment allows news imagery with its credit requirements and bounds uncertain reuse without a source-domain allowlist, watermark removal or invented permission.

evals.name: prose-timeline-is-not-a-site
evals.prompt: Give me a five-bullet chronological outline of the events in this supplied LeaseCo note. Plain text only; I am not asking for a website or downloadable files.
evals.expected_output: A short evidence-bounded prose outline, with no project folders, asset acquisition, site generation or unnecessary subagents.

assertions.text: The answer remains prose and does not create files or start a website workflow.
The answer does not invent five distinct dated corporate events when the supplied evidence contains fewer.

evals.name: failed-isolation-keeps-the-photograph
evals.prompt: We are continuing an investigative timeline website. The licensed news portrait is excellent, but every background-removal attempt destroys the person's hair and glasses. There is no usable cutout. The original framed photograph looks good, and a cheap image model could invent a cleaner face. Decide what to put on the page and how to credit it; save a short decision to outputs/decision.md. Do not edit images, call a paid tool or build the site in this decision step.
evals.expected_output: Retain an intentionally framed authentic photograph rather than discarding documentary imagery, inventing a face or pretending an opaque crop is a cutout. Credit the source and actual modifications.

assertions.text: The decision keeps the authentic framed photograph and explicitly identifies it as the fallback for failed isolation, not a successful cutout.
No synthetic face or alteration of documentary identity is proposed, and no paid operation occurs.
The decision retains reader-visible source credit and records actual editorial modifications without inventing licence details.
